regions.location: Upper-left oblique red branch; text along its outer edge
regions.grammar_rationale: Two adverbs: similiter = similarly, hic = here. This is a short relational/deictic direction, not an ordinary noun phrase. No elided verb is supplied.
regions.uncertainty: The writing is oblique; the ordinary expansion is not used to add an object or action.

regions.location: Upper-right oblique red branch, text following the branch
regions.grammar_rationale: A possible repetition of a relational cue is visible, but the whole inscription is not securely read.
regions.uncertainty: Several following words and the exact beginning/end remain unreadable. No completion from S01.

regions.location: Vertical writing above/left of the central figure enclosure
regions.grammar_rationale: No reliable complete grammatical expression.
regions.uncertainty: Orientation and abbreviation prevent a secure reading; relation to the curved inscription below is uncertain.

regions.location: Curving inscription around the central small human figure, including both flanks and lower arc
regions.grammar_rationale: The full run cannot be securely segmented or assigned nominal/sentential grammar.
regions.uncertainty: hic is only tentative in this region; do not merge confidently with S03 or infer anatomy from the depicted figure.

regions.location: Short horizontal line left of the upper left rounded compartment
regions.grammar_rationale: If read correctly, ad with a gerundival expression indicates purpose; the missing head prevents a full grammatical reading.
regions.uncertainty: Could be a prose rubric or a separate short instruction rather than an anatomical label; middle word unreadable.

regions.location: Short three/four-line block outside the upper right main compartment
regions.grammar_rationale: A compact prose fragment is visible, but no reliable complete clause is transcribed.

regions.location: Three-line inscription inside the lower small right circle

expansion_candidates.note: Final nasal expansion/ending tentative; intervening words unexpanded.

regions.grammar_rationale: Tentative but visible fluit is a finite verb; unde is relational and hic is deictic. On this reading the inscription contains a clause, even though its full wording is uncertain.
regions.uncertainty: Do not treat the whole inscription or semen ending as securely transcribed. The middle line cannot be completed.

expansion_candidates.note: Normalized ae and v/u separated from the visible reading; final word not supplied.

regions.grammar_rationale: Visible est suggests a copular clause: this is a/the way ...; subject/referent and final complement remain unresolved.
regions.uncertainty: The last word is not confidently readable. No particular bodily fluid or channel asserted.

regions.location: Short horizontal writing across the rounded top/cap of the long central stem
regions.grammar_rationale: Possible et is insufficient to recover the whole expression or to establish that et is an isolated label.
regions.uncertainty: Some writing crosses/abuts the cap contour; no ownership is assigned solely by proximity.

regions.location: Horizontal inscription immediately under the cap inside the central stem

expansion_candidates.note: Tentative candidate only; not a resolved diplomatic reading.

regions.grammar_rationale: hic is legible; the remaining word may be a finite passive verb. Relational/sentential classification is provisional and must not be counted as a secure clause.
regions.uncertainty: Several medial and final letters uncertain; comprimitur is a reading candidate, not established text.

regions.location: Small outlined circle to the left of the central stem
regions.grammar_rationale: Similarly here: adverbial/deictic direction; no noun phrase and no inferred finite verb.
regions.uncertainty: Exact abbreviation glyph is represented descriptively as [abbr], not replaced silently by expanded letters.

regions.location: Rounded header of the long left outer vertical band
regions.grammar_rationale: Adverbial/deictic expression, with no lexical noun. Its spatial isolation is clear.

regions.location: Rounded header of the long right outer vertical band

expansion_candidates.note: Final letters/abbreviation resolution less secure than collum.

regions.grammar_rationale: collum is a noun; matricis, if the tentative ending is right, is a dependent genitive: neck of the womb. This is nominal grammar, not an identification of the neighboring drawn object by location alone.
regions.uncertainty: Complete ending of the second word is not secure; no broader anatomical claim is supplied.

assessment.secure_minimum: F13V contains spatially isolated adverbial/deictic similiter hic readings (including abbreviated occurrences), so at least these inscriptions are not ordinary noun phrases. No finite verb is invented to turn them into full sentences.
assessment.nominal_evidence: F13V collum matric[?], tentatively expanded collum matricis, supports a nominal-expression candidate with a less secure second-word ending.
assessment.sentence_evidence: Several additional regions may contain copular/finite clauses (hec est uia..., fluit..., hic ...), but their confidence differs and incomplete words remain explicit. They are not all secure translations.
assessment.f22v_capacity: No isolated short inscription securely identified; running prose inside/around a diagram does not itself establish label grammar.
assessment.index_capacity: No secure independent SINGLE_SIGN_OR_INDEX region detected on the opened Bodleian frames; no Arabic material opened. This is absence of a detected example in these frames, not a universal claim.
assessment.claim_limit: These two selected external images establish neither a calibrated grammar distribution nor any Voynich word. Relation-like short inscriptions prevent a universal nominal-only rule; they do not identify AND, HOURS or any target meaning.
assessment.independence_limit: Same-model machine native vision, not an expert paleographic reading or independent historical confirmation. Do not resolve disagreements by majority vote.
